entities.summary: Hakor, also known as Hagar or Achoris, was an ancient Egyptian pharaoh of the 29th Dynasty, ruling for 13 years from approximately 395 to 382 BCE. His reign marked the apex of this feeble and short-lived dynasty, which ultimately collapsed due to internal power struggles and external pressures. Hakor's short tenure was marked by a series of costly military campaigns against neighboring kingdoms, including the Assyrians and the Persians. Despite these efforts, Egypt's economy continued to decline, and the dynasty's very existence was threatened. Hakor's legacy is largely forgotten, overshadowed by the more prominent figures of his time, but his reign provides valuable insight into the complexities of ancient Egyptian politics and the challenges faced by this once-mighty civilization. As the ancient Greek historian Herodotus noted, 'Hakor was a man of great wealth and power, but his reign was also marked by great instability and conflict.'
